judgment.rationale: Both indicators sit at the same BASIC 1 coordinate (rank 0), so direction rests on substantive content rather than rank. B1.2.2.1.3 (Reading / Sub-Strand 2: Phonics, under Content Standard B1.2.2.1 'Connect sounds to letters and blend letters/syllables in order to read and write') asks learners to understand the relationship between the spelling of words and speech sounds — i.e. grapheme-phoneme knowledge. B1.5.10.1.1 (Using Writing Conventions/Grammar Usage / Sub-Strand 10: Spelling) requires learners to identify and spell simple words correctly, and its own parent Content Standard is explicitly 'Use phonics knowledge to spell words' (B1.5.10.1), with LC tags 'phonics', 'spell', 'words'. The curriculum therefore states that the spelling-production indicator draws on exactly the sound-spelling understanding expressed by the phonics indicator, so proficiency in the second supports success in the first. This is application of phonics understanding to accurate spelling, not mere repeated wording ('words', 'spelling').
